officialX402Flow.quoteStep: Fetch the paid URL without a payment header and read the HTTP 402 quote.
officialX402Flow.paymentStep: Use a buyer-owned x402 client or wallet to create PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, then retry the same method, URL, body, and content-type. Legacy X-PAYMENT and PAYMENT remain compatible.
officialX402Flow.successStep: Treat HTTP 200 paid JSON plus PAYMENT-RESPONSE or compatible receipt headers as settlement evidence.
officialX402Flow.clientLibraryPattern: wrapFetchWithPayment(fetch, protocolClient) retries with a payment header after local quote checks pass.
officialX402Flow.sameRequestRule: Retry the exact same request shape after adding payment: method, URL, body, and content-type must not drift.

officialQuoteToPaymentChecklist: Step 1: request without a payment header and read the HTTP 402 PAYMENT-REQUIRED quote; tolerate X-PAYMENT-REQUIRED from legacy servers.
Step 2: create PAYMENT-SIGNATURE from the 402 accept requirement in a buyer-owned wallet or x402 client; X-PAYMENT and PAYMENT remain legacy-compatible.
Step 3: retry the same URL with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and keep method, body, and content-type unchanged.
Step 4: confirm HTTP 200 plus PAYMENT-RESPONSE, legacy X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE, or x-x402 receipt headers.
If payment still fails, call x402-payment-failure-doctor with url, method, status, payment header presence, verify status, settle status, and response headers.

quoteToSettleGoal.reason: The canary has no request body, no upstream model dependency, and the smallest public price, so payment failures are easier to diagnose.
